candidate.selection_reason: user-controlled hostname parameter -> unsanitized interpolation into shell command -> potential command injection vulnerability
candidate.source_summary: hostname parameter passed to resolve function
candidate.sink_summary: shell.exec(cmd, {silent: true}) executes the constructed command
candidate.guard_summary: No sanitization or validation of hostname before interpolation into shell command. The dns-lookup-script.js uses process.argv[2] directly in dns.lookup() but the shell command construction is vulnerable.
candidate.risk_pattern: User-controlled hostname parameter is directly interpolated into shell command without sanitization, allowing command injection via shell metacharacters
candidate.context_summary: The resolve function takes hostname parameter, constructs a shell command using util.format with nodeBinary, scriptPath, and hostname, then executes it via shell.exec. The script dns-lookup-script.js uses dns.lookup() but the vulnerability is in the shell command construction.
unresolved_facts: How the resolve function is called and what controls exist on the hostname parameter at call sites

target_cwe.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
target_cwe.description: The product constructs all or part of an OS command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended OS command when it is sent to a downstream component. This weakness can lead to a vulnerability in environments in which the attacker does not have direct access to the operating sy...
target_cwe.impact: code execution, data access, data modification
remediation_steps: Use parameterized queries and prepared statements
Implement strict input validation with whitelisting
